intro.opening: The only surviving wonder of the ancient world, in the morning while the air is still cool. This is the shared-departure version: a small group, a licensed Egyptologist guide, an air-conditioned vehicle, and the three pyramids and the Great Sphinx before the plateau heats up and the coaches arrive. By early to mid-afternoon you're back at your hotel.
intro.whyThisOrder: The early start is the point: you reach the plateau before it heats and before the coaches arrive. Your guide moves the group through the three pyramids in sequence, then the panorama viewpoint, then the Sphinx and its valley temple. Two to three hours on the plateau is enough to absorb the scale without losing the group to the heat.
intro.returnNote: by early to mid-afternoon, at your hotel
fitFor: are visiting for the first time, with a single Cairo morning
want the Old Kingdom canon read by a qualified guide
prefer a shared departure with a small group
worthKnowing: It's a half day, about 5 to 6 hours.
The drive to the plateau takes roughly thirty to forty-five minutes, depending on the morning traffic.
You spend two to three hours on the plateau, in a group.
intro.closingLine: The reason the day still matters is the same reason it has always mattered: standing in front of the thing.

stops.title: Pickup from your hotel
stops.text: Pickup from your hotel, then the drive to the Giza Plateau through the morning traffic, roughly thirty to forty-five minutes depending on the day.

stops.title: The three pyramids
stops.text: The Great Pyramid of Khufu, completed around 2560 BC, stood at 146 metres for the next four thousand years, built from about 2.3 million blocks aligned to true north. Khafre's, slightly smaller and on higher ground, still carries a band of original white Tura limestone casing at the apex. Menkaure's, the smallest, finishes the line.

stops.title: The panorama viewpoint
stops.text: From the pyramids, your guide takes the group on to the panorama viewpoint.

stops.title: The Great Sphinx and its valley temple
stops.text: The Sphinx sits at the plateau's eastern edge, carved from a single limestone outcrop, generally dated to Khafre's reign around 2500 BC. It is the largest monolithic statue in the world. The missing nose has nothing to do with Napoleon's artillery, despite the legend.
